lessons.title: Unselfish Heroes

memory_verse.text: Give generously to him and do so without a grudging heart; then because of this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.

getting_started: God doesn't bless us so we can be selfish. God's plan is always for us to share – whether from our abundance or our poverty. Being generous isn't limited to material things; it extends to our time, skills and talents, even our relationship. As you prepare for this study, determine with God's help to develop the generous spirit He desires for you to have.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: See Teacher Guide. Discuss with students the following questions:

overview: How those even in poverty have something to offer God's kingdom.
That the key principle of godly giving are obedience and selflessness.
How being good managers of our resources glorifies God.

discussion.heading: Giving from Poverty (The Widow at Zarephath)

questions.text: Read and summarize 1 Kings 17:7-16. Why do you think God chose a poverty-stricken widow to supply Elijah's needs?
questions.leader_note: Note: How much we have, or don't have, isn't the issue. The real issue is our willingness to share it with others.

questions.text: Why do you think she was instructed to make bread first for Elijah and bring it to him, and then make a meal for herself and her son?
questions.leader_note: Note: When God gives specific directions, He has a specific purpose for them.

questions.text: Why do you think God also requires the poor to give to others when they don't even have enough for themselves?
What can you offer generously give to those in need? Besides giving money, what other ways can you [truncated in photo].
Read and summarize 1 Kings 18:1-16. What does Obadiah's life teach us about our attitudes toward possessions?
questions.leader_note: Note: We should view our possessions as a means to minister to others.

questions.text: Which act of generosity was greater: Obadiah providing for hundred prophets or the widow feeding Elijah? Why?
What does it mean to have a generous heart, and why is it important, especially for Christians?
What is the connection between obedience and selflessness? How do these two characteristics relate to giving?
Read Deut 15:7-11. List some specific "dos and don'ts" from this passage in regard to treatment of the needy. List ways in which you can minister to your peers who have less.

lessons.act: What is your current level of generosity? Ask God to speak to you about one way in which you can grow in giving. Then follow through with His instruction.

invitation_option.label: Invitation Option
invitation_option.text: Jesus modelled for us the ultimate act of generosity when He gave His own life to save ours. If you've never accepted that gift, do it today, and receive the generous gift of salvation, forgiveness from sin, and promise of eternity in heaven. See pg2 (ABC of Salvation) for guidance.

lessons.title: Desperate Heroes

memory_verse.text: Blessed is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God… He upholds the cause of the oppressed and gives food to the hungry. The LORD sets prisoners free

getting_started: In today's society, people tend to look out for themselves, even at the expense of others. But God has called us to a life of heroic proportions. This lesson comes to remind us that heroes aren't just found in front pages of newspapers or in the pages of the Bible – they can be found in our very own mirrors. As we trust God in the midst of desperate circumstances, we will become heroes for His kingdom.
overview: How God is aware of our circumstances and planning our rescue.
Why believers must never lose the desire to help others.
The fact that God can be trusted to fulfill His Word.

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 6:24-25; 7:1-8. Why were the lepers willing to risk their lives to go to the enemy's camp?
questions.leader_note: Note: The most risky option actually held the most hope for them.

questions.text: How did God use the lepers' difficult situation to bring about good?
questions.leader_note: Note: God sees the big picture. As we trust Him and step out in faith, He is able to change both our perspectives and our circumstances.

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 7:9-11. How did the lepers react to their incredible discovery? Would your actions have been similar or different? Why?
questions.leader_note: Note: See the Teacher Guide; there's an informative note after these questions that tells how lepers were treated in ancient times.

questions.text: Do you think the four lepers were heroes? Why or why not?
questions.leader_note: Note: By acknowledging that keeping the news to themselves wouldn't be right, the lepers chose to help end the suffering of those inside the city by telling them that food was available and the enemy had fled.

questions.text: What good news can you share with others?
questions.leader_note: Note: Believers can share the good news of Christ's love and forgiveness.

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 7:12-20. Why do you think the king didn't initially believe the good news? What convinced him?
Why do people today doubt the good news of God's Word and His plan to rescue them? What could help convince them to at least investigate the claims of Christianity?
questions.leader_note: Note: If unbelievers have the opportunity to get to know and trust those who claim to be Christians, they might be willing to trust Christ for themselves.

questions.text: Read Psalm 146:3-9. How does knowing that God cares for and watches over those in difficult circumstances affect our willingness to take risks for Him? What kinds of risks have you taken? What kinds of risks might He call you to take?
Reread Psalm 146:7-9, and note whom God helps and how He helps them. Also identify whom God doesn't help.
questions.leader_note: Note: God can be trusted in every situation. He "remains faithful forever" (v6).

lessons.act: Were there times in your life when you felt despair because of your circumstances? What were those circumstances about? Is there any current struggles that have left you feeling desperate? What are they about? Bring them to God in prayer, and ask Him for courage to trust Him and make right decisions. Pray also that God will use you this week to bring hope and relief to others who are hurting.

lessons.title: A Truthful Hero

memory_verse.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

getting_started: The world in which we live elevates and admires certain individuals who are attractive, gifted, and physically strong. Hero status is often granted with little regard for things like truthfulness and integrity. But God doesn't view people and situations the way society sees them. He is looking for people who will live out His truth and faithfully proclaim it to a lost world. This study comes to challenge you to be that kind of hero – starting now.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: As believers, we must be faithful to communicate God's truth to others so they can receive the ultimate reward: God's gift of eternal life.

illustration_option.label: Illustration Option
illustration_option.note: By making Bible study and practice a priority, you'll be able to recognize messages that don't line up with God's Word.

overview: Our responsibility to communicate God's truth to those around us.
What it means to correctly handle God's Word.
How we can recognize people who falsely claim to speak for God.

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 22:8-14. Why do you think the king wanted to hear from God?
Why should we be interested in knowing what God thinks of our actions?
questions.leader_note: Note: No matter what other people think of us, God's opinion is the only one that truly matters.

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 22:15-20. What were some of the dangers involved with being a prophet, especially one who brought bad news to a ruler?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Prophets were often hated, threatened, persecuted, imprisoned, and even killed for speaking God's truth. (see also 1 Kings 18:4; 19:1-3; 2 Chron 24:20-22; Jer 38:6; and Luke 11:48).

questions.text: What's the difference between "sugar-coating" something and expressing the truth in love?
Read 2 Tim 2:15. What do you think it means to correctly handle God's Word?
What would be an example of someone mishandling God's Word?
questions.leader_note: Hint: This could be using the Scripture to try to prove or defend an unbiblical position, deliberately taking verses out of context, denying the Bible's teaching, etc.

questions.text: Read Jer 23:25-32. What can happen when a person mixes truth with a lie?
questions.leader_note: Note: We must be careful to examine the whole message to see if what was said is true.

questions.text: How can you know whether someone is really speaking God's truth?
questions.leader_note: Hint: While God still speaks through people, He will not tell anyone to say or do something that contradicts His Word in any way. The Bible tells us to "test" or "prove" everything to see whether or not it is from God (1 John 4:1).

questions.text: Why is it important to be truthful with a person who asks for spiritual advice, even when the truth may be painful?
questions.leader_note: Hint: When we give spiritual advice, we represent God and must be true to His Word. Being truthful with people can also help us spare them from harm later.

lessons.act: Review 2 Tim 2:15, today's key verse. It's important to handle God's Word correctly. As such, we should be principled in our lives so that others can come to know God and follow Him. Now take a few moments to silently reflect on how you've been handling God's Word, repenting where needed, and asking God to give you clarity and boldness to know and share the good news with others this week.

lessons.title: A Courageous Hero

memory_verse.text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.

getting_started: No one, not even heroes, are immune to the effects of fear. But we should be careful not to let fear get in the way of what we can do for God. From all confirmations, courage is not the absence of fear, but the ability to withstand and even overcome it. Fear tells us to do what's convenient and "safe." But a hero does what's right, regardless of personal consequences. This study comes to encourage you to stand up to your fears.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: With God's help, we can conquer our fears so that they don't control our lives.

overview: What it means to be courageous.
How unhealthy fear can hinder our service to God.
How to overcome fear so we can become all that God has called us to be.

questions.text: Read Jer 38:1-6. Why did the king's officials not want to hear Jeremiah's message?
How is this similar to the attitudes of many people today?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Many people today don't want to hear God's warning. They prefer to go their own ways and believe that everything will be fine regardless of their personal choices.

questions.text: Read Jer 38:7-13. What do Ebed-Melech's actions reveal about his character?
questions.leader_note: Note: It took courage for Ebed-Melech to do what was right in spite of the potential consequences.

questions.text: What is our responsibility as Christians when we see someone being treated unfairly?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We should do what we can to make the situation better, always relying on God and responding obediently as He directs us.

questions.text: Read Jer 39:15-18. What rewards do you think Christians can expect if they obey God and properly confront the injustices around them?

discussion.heading: Fear Factor
discussion.note: God's Word repeatedly instructs us not to fear. Unhealthy fear can paralyze us spiritually and keep us from moving forward in our relationship with God. But faith sets us free to fulfill God's will, God promises to take care of His children. Whatever we face, we can know that God cares about our situation and is already working on our behalf

questions.text: Read 2 Kings 6:11-17. Why do people struggle with unhealthy fear, just like Elisha's servant did?
Read Proverbs 29:25. What does this passage say about unhealthy fear?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Unhealthy fear is like a snare. But those who trust God can rest assured that He is watching over them.

questions.text: Read Luke 12:6-7. Why must we put aside fear and trust God?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Because God loves us and promises to care for us and meet our needs, we have nothing to fear.

lessons.act: List on a paper several types of injustices involving individuals or people groups. (Examples could include a friend being ostracised by other students, people in your community being denied certain rights, etc.) Then describe the risks involved in stepping into each situation to help defend the individuals who are being treated unjustly. Do also write the situations in a way that would please and glorify God. Note: Getting in touch with the Holy Spirit through prayer gives us courage to face any trial, and daily Bible study gives us the wisdom to know what to say and do.

lessons.title: The Reality Of Miracles

memory_verse.text: Jesus then took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted. He did the same with the fish.

getting_started: Many Christians talk about miracles, believe in them, and sometimes pray for them, but seldom experience them first-hand. Perhaps it's too easy, even tempting, to look for natural solutions when faced with problems. Yet, Jesus is still the same yesterday, today and forever; He still does supernatural things in the lives of people. Today's study will help you form a solid foundation for your belief in Jesus' supernatural power.
overview: That Jesus is able and willing to do miracles in our lives because He cares about the needs and issues we face every day.
That God wants us to be involved in miracles through our faith and actions.
That no need is too big for God; He does things beyond our imaginations.

questions.text: Read the following passages and list what Jesus demonstrates power over in each passage: Matt 8:23-27 | Matt 8:28-34 | Matt 8:14-17 | Luke 7:12-15.
Read John 6:1-7. What was Jesus' response when He saw the crowd of people coming toward Him? Why do you think He responded this way?
questions.leader_note: Note: Jesus cares about our needs, no matter how great or small they might seem.

questions.text: What are some reasons people might think Jesus wouldn't be able to see or care about their needs?
questions.leader_note: Note: While Jesus is the almighty Son of God, He is also our closest friend. And He cares about what we're experiencing.

discussion.heading: He wants to involve us … [page 018 not supplied]

questions.text: [page 018 not supplied]

lessons.title: The Reasons For Miracles

memory_verse.text: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.

getting_started: Have you ever seen a miracle? If so, how did it affect your life? Today's study explores the reasons for miracles. As you examine through this study why Jesus does the supernatural, you'll realize that you need to believe God for miracles – not just for your benefit, but for the benefit of those around you. As you prepare for this study, pray that God will reveal His power in your life.
overview: The reason Jesus did miracles while on earth.
The reason Jesus does miracles today.
How our lives and ministries could be impacted when we experience God's supernatural power.

questions.text: Miracles bring glory to God. Read John 9:1-7. Why would a miracle bring glory to God?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Miracles bring glory to God because it is through miracles that people get to know who Jesus is and what He can do.

questions.text: Miracles prove that Jesus is God's Son. Read following passages and answer the corresponding questions:

bullets.title: Luke 5:17-26
bullets.text: Why did Jesus come to earth in the first place? How did the healing of the man relate to Jesus' mission?

bullets.title: John 10:37-38
bullets.text: What attitude did some of the people have toward Jesus and His teaching? What should have changed their attitude?

questions.text: Miracles lead people to eternal life. Read John 20:30-31. Describe what part miracles play in fulfilling Jesus' mission.
questions.leader_note: Note: Miracles are a powerful way to convince skeptics that Jesus wasn't just a good man and a good teacher – He is the Son of God.

questions.text: Miracles demonstrate Jesus' compassion. Read Matt 20:29-34; Mark 1:40-42. Identify the miracles that happened in these passages and what motivated Jesus to perform those miracles.
questions.leader_note: Note: Even when we feel rejected by everyone, we can be assured that Jesus cares enough to help.

questions.text: Why do you think it means for unbelievers to see miracles among Christians?
Why might miracles be especially effective in a society where every religion is seen as an equally valid way to truth?
questions.leader_note: Hint: When miracles are seen in our ministries, it forces people to consider the possibility that what we're saying is true. This can be the first step to them accepting Christ into their lives.

questions.text: What do you think it would take to see more miracles characterizing Christians' lives today?
Read John 14:13-14. Do you think these verses mean that Jesus will do whatever we ask Him to do, no matter what it is? Explain.
questions.leader_note: Hint: Jesus was making the point that prayer brings supernatural power and is consistent with His character. As such, when we have legitimate needs and hurts, He is willing to help us in miraculous ways.

lessons.act: God wants you to pray and believe for miracles on a regular basis. It's part of His plan for your life. But this kind of lifestyle doesn't happen without practice. You need to make a habit of praying for friends and family when you see problems that seem impossible. And when you face situations that seems to have no answer, practice making prayer your first response rather than your last. Note that God will sometimes answer in ways that are much different from our expectations, but He will always act in our best interest and for His glory. Then take a few moments to pray, asking for divine intervention on specific needs you are facing, trusting God for answers.

lessons.title: The Responses To Miracles

memory_verse.text: Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight; your faith has healed you." Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, praising God. When all the people saw it, they also praised God.

getting_started: For Christians, few things are more thrilling than seeing or experiencing a miracle. Even a testimony of such an event can build our faith and lead us into great times of worship. But not everybody reacts to reality of miracles in that way. This study is designed to help you recognize that fact so you, too, can develop appropriate responses to Jesus – and to others.
overview: The various ways people respond to miracles.
Why some people refuse to believe that miracles even exist.
How Christians should respond when faced with a situation that calls for a miracle.

questions.text: Read Matt 9:27-34. Why do you think Pharisees said Jesus did miracles through demonic power?
questions.leader_note: Note: The Pharisees couldn't deny Jesus' miracles, but they refused to believe that Jesus was who He claimed to be.

questions.text: Why are some people today sceptical about Jesus doing miracles?
questions.leader_note: Note: Some will refuse to believe miracles regardless of the evidence (Luke 16:31). They look for excuses to explain away God's work. We must be ready to deal with these arguments. That way, our faith will remain strong, and we get the chance to share Christ with others by putting His love on display.

questions.text: Read Luke 6:6-11. (The Pharisees saw Jesus as a threat to their powerful religious system. They were preoccupied with removing Jesus as a threat.) Why are some people today resistant to miracles?
Read Luke 18:35-43. Why do you think the crowd wanted the blind man to be quiet?

discussion.heading: Faith and Praise
discussion.note: It is hard to pray over and over for a miracle when nothing seems to happen. Times like these challenge our faith and endurance. Rather than lose faith, we must continue to depend on God and worship Him until an answer comes. God will never let us down.

questions.text: Read Matt 8:5-13. What does it mean to have faith in Jesus?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It means accepting who Jesus is and what He can do.

questions.text: What kinds of things might inspire you to have faith in Jesus for miracles?
questions.leader_note: Hint: You may have seen Him do amazing things; you believe that He cares about people; you believe the promises in His Word.

questions.text: Read Luke 13:10-13. Why do you think the woman's first response to being healed was praising God?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Worship comes from a heart of gratitude.

questions.text: When is it easiest for you to praise God and what He has done for you?

lessons.act: Take a few moments to consider the kinds of attitudes you have when praying for yourself or others. It's often easy to forget what a serious and important thing prayer is. Resolve not to allow that to happen to you. Now, spend a few minutes in prayer, ask God to increase your faith and give you the right attitudes and responses. Talk to him about specific needs in your life and in the lives of family and friends, trusting Him for intervention. Finally, take time to praise God for His compassion, care, and faithfulness.

lessons.title: A Different World

memory_verse.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.

getting_started: Though we live in a rapidly changing culture, some things remain the same. The challenges Joshua and the Israelites faced in ancient times are not unlike some of the issues we must deal with today. As the Israelites prepared to enter the Promised Land, they faced encounters with false religions and cultures very different from their own. To be successful in their new home, they would need to depend on God and stay true to His Word. Likewise, we need to make God the centre of our lives so we can continue to stand strong for Christ.
overview: How the Israelites' lives were changing as they prepared to enter the Promised Land.
How a pagan prostitute took part in God's promise by turning from her sinful culture and teaming up with God's people.
Why it's important to acknowledge God, remember His work in our lives, and depend on Him for strength as we live out our Christianity in a changing world.

questions.text: Read Joshua 1:1-4. In what ways were the Israelites' lives changing?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It was a new generation; only Joshua and Caleb were left of all the adults who left Egypt during the Exodus (Num 14:1-35). b. They had a new leader and must adjust to his leadership; for Moses had died. c. They now have new land to call theirs, even the land God promised Abraham. d. They had nations to conquer in order to gain control of that new land. e. They were finally settling as a nation.

questions.text: Read Joshua 1:6-9. What did God tell Joshua to do in order to be successful in the new land?
In your opinion, what are some of the biggest temptations teens today face? How can spending time in God's Word help you avoid temptation?
questions.leader_note: Note: God's Word will show you how to live temptation-free and will spiritually strengthen you.

discussion.heading: Choose God's Side
discussion.leader_note: Hint: No matter what kind of challenge we're facing, we'll find success when we choose to be on God's side. We align ourselves with Him by obeying His commands and advancing His purposes.

questions.text: Read and summarize Joshua 2:1-14. What would have happened if Rahab had maintained allegiance to pagan gods instead of helping Israel?
questions.leader_note: Hint: God would accomplish God and His servants, she and her family would have certainly been destroyed along with the rest of Jericho.

questions.text: How can we know what God wants us to do when we have a tough decision to make?
questions.leader_note: Hint: God's plans and directions are evident in His Word. Study His Word, communicate with Him through prayer, and seek the counsel of trusted Christians.

questions.text: Read Joshua 4:4-11. Why did the Israelites take stones from the Jordan?
questions.leader_note: Hint: In the new land, they would encounter many religions. They needed to remember that the LORD is the one true God who sustained them in the wilderness, brought them through the Jordan, and gave them their inheritance.

questions.text: Make a list of things you can do to acknowledge and remember God's work in your life.

lessons.act: List some cultural influences in today's world that can make it hard to stay on track spiritually. Your strength is not a match for those influences. So, always be dependent on God's strength, not your own. Take a few minutes to pray, asking God to give you strength to resist temptation as you remember and acknowledge Him in every part of your life.

lessons.title: Getting The Message

memory_verse.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve: whether ye will serve the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

getting_started: As they entered into their new home, the Israelites were exposed to pagan cultures and strange philosophies that could distract them from serving God. We too face similar challenge today: From the classrooms to the chat rooms, we are exposed to a grab bag of competing and contradictory messages. But when we make up our minds to serve the LORD no matter what messages come our way, God can do some amazing things in our lives. As you prepare for this study, pray that the message of serving God will get into your heart in a fresh and powerful way.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: God's message calls us to seek a relationship with Christ and live with eternity in mind.

overview: The importance of paying attention to God's message.
How Achan disregarded God's instruction and paid a high price for his rebellion.
How to avoid the mistake of falling for the world's message.
What we must do to keep worldly things from becoming idols in our lives.

questions.text: Read Joshua 5:13-15; 6:1-5. In what ways were the messenger's instruction unusual?
questions.leader_note: Note: The messenger didn't offer any recognizable military strategy. The residents of Jericho might have thought it foolish for the Israelites to march around their city for 6 days without making any further advances. Nevertheless, their walls did come down.

questions.text: Read 1 Cor 1:18, 23-25. In what ways might some people view Christ's message as unusual or difficult to understand?
Read Joshua 6:17-19. What were Joshua's instructions to the Israelites concerning the things in Jericho?
Read Joshua 7:1-9. What went wrong at Ai?
Read Joshua 7:10-26. What worldly pattern or message did Achan follow and what was the result?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Achan wanted what he was willing to do anything to get them – even if it meant breaking God's commands and dragging others into his sin. Because he failed to listen to God, he brought trouble to Israel and destruction to himself and his family.

questions.text: Read Joshua 23:1-7, 14-16. What instructions did Joshua give to the Israelites in those verses? Why was it necessary they heed those instructions?
questions.leader_note: Note: As long as the Israelites obeyed His commands, God would bless and protect them. But if they turned from the truth to worship idols, they would be destroyed.

questions.text: Read Joshua 24:14-16, 19-23. List how you can keep the attractions of the world from becoming idols that get in the way of your relationship with God.
questions.leader_note: Hint: 1. We either accept God's message and follow Him, or we, like Achan, buy into the world's lies and rush headlong into destruction. So, Choose God and His message. 2. Is there anything that you wouldn't be willing to give up for God? If so, ask God to change your heart until your love for Him is greater than your desire for anything else.

lessons.act: Note that an idol is anything that is given greater priority than your relationship with God. Spend a few moments in prayer, asking God to remove any unhealthy desires from your life.

invitation_option.label: Invitation Option
invitation_option.text: The most important message in the Bible is that of forgiveness and eternal life through Christ. If you haven't accepted Jesus as your Saviour and Lord, He wants you to do so today, even now. See page 2 (ABC of Salvation) for guidance.

lessons.title: When People Give In To Peer Pressure

memory_verse.text: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.

getting_started: Sometimes peer pressure can feel a bit like getting caught in a stampede. At first, people follow those around them because it seems like the right thing to do – after all, "everyone else" is doing it. But before they know it, they find themselves being pulled along by the crowd. As you prepare, ask God to give you strength to resist negative peer pressure and to place in your heart a desire to please and obey Him above all else.
overview: Wanting to be like everyone else can have negative spiritual effects.
Seeking others approval can cause us to miss out on God's approval.
Following people instead of God has disastrous results.
Our choice of friends will greatly affect the pressures we face.

discussion.heading: Wanting to Be Like Everyone Else

questions.text: Make a list of things teens are pressured by peers to do and ways their behaviour is affected by those things. Why are these actions and behaviours sometimes difficult to resist.
Read 1 Sam 8:4-7, 18-20. How can wanting to be like everyone else affect us spiritually?
questions.leader_note: Note: Negative peer pressure can draw us away from a relationship with God.

questions.text: Read John 12:42-43. Why did some of the leaders who believed in Jesus refuse to confess their faith in Him?
What did they give up to gain the approval of others?
questions.leader_note: Hint: They sacrificed the chance to follow and learn from Jesus, and they missed out on receiving God's approval. They probably did not make it to heaven – Matt 10:32-33.

questions.text: In what ways do many teens today make the same mistake?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Some hide their relationship with Jesus or give it up because they're afraid of what others might think. In doing so, they sacrifice the chance to experience God's plan for their lives and influence others for Him. They may also lose their salvation.

questions.text: Read 1 Kings 13:1-24. How can you know when to listen to what others are telling you? When should you use caution?
questions.leader_note: Hint: When God has placed others in our lives – such as parents, church leaders, and even Christian friends – who can steer us in the right direction as we learn to live according to God's will. But we must be careful not to follow people who encourage us to disobey God's commands, regardless of who they are or how credible they seem.

discussion.heading: Choosing the Wrong Crowd
discussion.leader_note: Note: Teens who yield to negative peer pressure often do so because they've picked their friends unwisely. The people we associate with may influence our lives in ways we do not expect.

questions.text: How can your friendships affect your behaviour in both positive and negative ways?
Read or summarize 1 Kings 12:1-16. What can happen to teens who follow the wrong crowd?
questions.leader_note: Hint: They may be influenced to use drugs or alcohol, become sexually promiscuous, join cult, drop out of school, etc.

questions.text: Note: If we choose unwise or ungodly friends, we'll be tempted to follow their poor examples.

lessons.act: God loves you and wants only what is best for you. Now, spend time in His presence and deepen your relationship with God. Then pray, ask God to reveal to you any addiction or unhealthy desires – whether it's an addiction or an unhealthy desire – and ask Him to strengthen you to make right choices.

lessons.title: Finding Your Centre

memory_verse.text: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.

getting_started: This study from the Book of Hebrews explores ancient Jewish roots of Christianity. This first study deals mainly with placing Christ at the centre of one's faith experience. As you prepare for this study, take a few moments to evaluate what occupies the centre of your own spiritual life. Revisiting your own spiritual history can help propel you into the future God has in store for you.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: Ignoring where our faith came from will ultimately confuse where it's headed.

overview: How the Book of Hebrews connects ancient spirituality with our current faith.
Why Jesus is the centre of our faith.
How to overcome temptations and approach God with boldness.

discussion.heading: Back in my day…
discussion.intro: Read Heb 1:1-4. The writer contrasted God's past communication through prophets with His current communication through His Son, who is the "exact representation" of God Himself.

questions.text: What do you know about the Old Testament and Judaism?
questions.leader_note: Note: The Old Testament explains God's first covenant or promise to His chosen people, the Jews. Through them, He revealed His Law – all the conditions His people were to live by to enjoy a proper relationship with Him.

questions.text: Why, according to Hebrews 1:1-4, was Jesus the only One capable of bringing salvation to humanity?
questions.leader_note: Note: Without the Old Testament law, we wouldn't have understood why Jesus' life and death were necessary.

discussion.heading: Oh, brother!
discussion.intro: Read Heb 2:9-11, 14-18. Jesus became human and experienced death in our place so we could come to God. Through His suffering, He related to us. And because He experienced a fully human life, He was able to overcome the power of sin and help us with our struggles.

questions.text: Why does it matter that Jesus lived on earth as a human being? How does that fact affect our lives?
How do you know when you're being tempted to do something God forbids?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We know temptation when we are tempted to do something God's Word says not to. Conscience, while not always dependable, will usually serve as an indication that something may not be right.

questions.text: How do you usually handle temptation? How well is your method working? What could you do to improve the situation?
questions.leader_note: Note: If we trust Jesus to provide a way out, He will give us satisfaction in choosing to do the right thing.

discussion.heading: Can we talk?
discussion.intro: Read Heb 4:14-16. Because Jesus overcame sin, He provides humanity access to God. His standing offer of grace gives us confidence to approach God. We don't have to waver in our faith, because He is there for us.

questions.text: List the different ways (tones and attitudes) in which people tend to approach or interact with God.
What might a person's approach to God indicate and what difference does it make?
questions.leader_note: Note: The way we approach God reveals much about our relationship with Him.

lessons.act: For a more in-depth approach to your study of Hebrews, over the next four weeks, read through the Book of Hebrews in a good study Bible, covering about two or three chapters per week. Find and look up all the Old Testament references in Hebrews; and ensure to keep track of your findings in a notebook. Hebrews contains approximately thirty-six quotations, thirty-five allusions, and fourteen references. That's why you'll need a study Bible; and you'll surely make some amazing discoveries that will help to strengthen your faith.

daily_dew_drops.title: The Image of the Invisible God

lessons.title: Understanding Your Saviour

memory_verse.text: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.

getting_started: This study looks at the ideas of the Old Testament blood sacrifice and the priesthood, and how they actually pointed to Jesus' sacrifice as the ultimate and perfect High Priest. It is on account of that which Jesus did as our High Priest that we're reconciled to God and can interact directly with Him. Ensure to take good advantage of the interactive questions in this lesson; they'll help you to access the real-life relevance of this study.
overview: How the Book of Hebrews explains spiritual salvation.
Why Jesus had to die for our sins.
How Jesus represents us before God the Father today.

questions.text: Read Heb 9:22, 26-28. What do you think is the difference between how the Old Testament dealt with sin's penalty and how the New Testament provided for it?
questions.leader_note: Hint: In the Old Testament, the problem of sin was temporarily addressed through a system of animal sacrifices. In the New Testament, the perfect sacrifice – Jesus Christ – accomplished what the blood of animal could not.

questions.text: Read Heb 12:14-16. What comes to mind when someone says the word "holy"?
questions.leader_note: Note: Living a holy life is an ongoing process of pursuing spiritually positive attitudes and actions.

questions.text: Why can living a holy life be so difficult sometimes? What behaviours, talk, and attitudes seem to give teens the most trouble? Why?
Read Heb 5:1-5. What are some of the differences between earthly priests and Christ – the ultimate High Priest?

Read Heb 9:6-15. What are some of the differences between the first tabernacle and the perfect system? [Hint: The first tabernacle was "not able" to clear the conscience of the worshipper (v9), but the perfect system, introduced by Jesus, is able to free people from sin (vv14-15).]
What do you think it means to view Jesus as your "High Priest"?
questions.leader_note: Note: Jesus is both your sacrifice and your only means of access to the Father.

questions.text: Read Heb 7:11, 18. How is the Priesthood of Jesus different from the typical Jewish priests of the Old Testament?
In what ways do people tend to rely on others – such as priests, pastors, friends, or family – for their experience with God?
questions.leader_note: Note: Those who think that someone else is responsible for their faith have an outdated understanding of religion and the priesthood.

questions.text: How could you help friends who rely on others' faith instead of interacting with God for themselves?

lessons.act: Read Heb 7:25; Romans 8:34. Before Jesus left this earth, He spent many hours in prayer for His people. After returning to heaven, He didn't abandon this priestly function. He continues to intercede to the Father for us, securing the help and provision we need to live for Him. It is important therefore that you think beyond an abstract view of Jesus' prayer and consider what He is actually doing for you right now. Note: It is one thing to say Jesus is your High Priest. It's quite another to thank Him for representing you before God. It's one thing to study Jesus' sacrifice. It's quite another to ask for forgiveness in your own life. It is important therefore that you commit to stay connected to God always.

lessons.title: Keeping Your Faith

memory_verse.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.

getting_started: Understanding deep spiritual concepts, such as those covered in the previous studies, does no good unless it leads to action. Today's study brings into focus the personal, real-life application of these concepts. Having been introduced to some of the theological truths in the Book of Hebrews, this study emphasizes the need for you to live an authentic life – a life that demonstrates agreement between your beliefs and your actions.
overview: We can resist temptation by depending on Jesus.
Choosing self-discipline and accepting God's discipline strengthens us.
Meeting together and encouraging each other build us as Christians.

questions.text: Read the following passages and answer the corresponding questions:

bullets.title: Heb 10:26-27, 30
bullets.text: What can people expect if they keep sinning?

bullets.title: Heb 12:1-3
bullets.text: What can sin do to us and how should we handle it? How can we keep from being distracted by sin? [Hint: Sin can tangle us up and keep us from doing what God has for us. We must continually combat wrongdoing by focusing on Jesus.]

questions.text: Read Heb 10:16-17. God promises to not judge us for our sins when we repent and turn from them. How can knowing this affect your choice to sin?
questions.leader_note: Note: If you take your relationship with Jesus serious, you'll rid your life of those issues that displease God – even if it's not the most popular thing to do.

questions.text: Read Heb 6:11-12. What does God want to prevent in our lives? What are some ways to avoid becoming lazy in our spiritual walk?
questions.leader_note: Note: It's better to stay spiritually healthy than to struggle during inevitable trials.

questions.text: Read Heb 12:4-11. According to this passage, why does God bring His discipline into our lives?
questions.leader_note: Note: God loves us enough to intervene when we let our relationship with Him slide. If we renew our commitment to Him, He will help us.

questions.text: Is being disciplined by an authority figure a good or bad thing? Why?
questions.leader_note: Note: Correction keeps us from harm. For example, a loving parent discipline a child reaching for the hot stove. The child is unaware of the potential injury, but God does. Similarly, we don't comprehend the consequences of our actions, but God does.

questions.text: Why is it better to be disciplined by God rather than be disciplined by a person?
Read Heb 3:12-13; 10:23-25. Why do some Christians stay away from Church these days?
How could you help Christian friends enjoy church more?
questions.leader_note: Note: People often underestimate the effects of kindness and encouragement. If you befriend people and genuinely make them feel welcome, peripheral issues tend to lose importance.

questions.text: Read Heb 4:12-13. In what way is it liberating to know that God knows us completely?
questions.leader_note: Note: Although we might feel uncomfortable about some of the things the Bible says or how it reveals sin in our lives, always keep in mind that God is for us. He gives us instruction so we can succeed.

lessons.act: Describe how encouraged you feel in Sunday School class. List some practical, realistic steps you could take to encourage other members of your class to keep attending Sunday School. Also list what you could do to encourage people who don't attend Sunday School to get involved in Teens Solution activities or Sunday School. Take a few minutes to pray, asking God for grace to encourage your friends and equally bring souls to Him.

lessons.title: Applying Your Confidence

memory_verse.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

getting_started: The topic of faith can stir quite a debate among Christians. While some define faith as absolute assurance in a particular outcome, others see it strictly as a reverent submission to the inevitable. This study attempts to balance these views, focusing on faith as it is described and defined in Hebrews 11. While it does explore supernatural forms of confidence, this "faith chapter" also examines what Christians are to do when things don't work out as expected.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: Genuine faith should have visible effects on our lives.

overview: What the Book of Hebrews says about faith.
How you can have more faith in your life.
How you can use faith to help others.

discussion.heading: God is worthy of our faith.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:1-3,6. Describe some ways people exercise faith.
questions.leader_note: Note: People often believe others love them. Though people can't "see" love, they have faith that it exists because of how those people have treated them.

questions.text: What determines the quality of someone's faith? That is, what makes the faith turn out good or bad?
questions.leader_note: Note: A person's faith is only as good as the person or the object in which it's placed.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:4-5, 7-8, 29-30. Using the accompanying questions as a guide, what can you learn from the examples of each of the following people in a way that demonstrate faith in God:

bullets.title: Abel
bullets.text: What are some sincere ways a teen could honour God that would require faith? What could a teen offer God that would cause Him to speak well of him or her as He did of Abel?

bullets.title: Enoch
bullets.text: In what ways do you think Enoch pleased God so much that God took him without his seeing death? How could we strive to please God in that way?

bullets.title: Noah
bullets.text: Considering Noah's example, how does your faith affect those around you?

bullets.title: Abraham
bullets.text: How do you know what actions to take when trusting God?

questions.text: What do you think most people mean when they say that faith is, or should be, a personal thing?
questions.leader_note: Hint: People often use this as an argument or excuse that people should keep their faith to themselves and not try to impose their beliefs on others.

discussion.heading: Faith brings power.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:32-35. Why might some of the miracles mentioned in this passage seem to require more faith or be more miraculous than the others?
Read Heb 11:35-40. What normally happens when people trust God and He doesn't do what they expect?
questions.leader_note: Note: We must not allow our circumstances to dictate our levels of faith; for God calls us to trust Him – not in a particular outcome.

questions.text: What should you do when you have faith in God and He allows something terrible to occur?

discussion.note: Having true faith does not mean knowing what's going to happen. Instead, it means trusting a situation to God and acting confidently on what He has told you – regardless of your situation. Therefore, one of the first step toward gaining more faith is taking the time and effort to listen to Him.

lessons.act: Read Romans 10:17. If faith comes by hearing, then what and whom we listen to does matter. If we want to increase our faith, we must honestly evaluate the sources of information and opinions we allow into our lives, no matter how harmless some of them might seem. So, we must determine by the Word of God to take control of our own outlook and refuse to let the world or circumstance decide how we should think and act.

lessons.title: Change Your Perspective

memory_verse.text: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

getting_started: Not everything is exactly as it seems on the surface – especially in spiritual matters. Some things that may seem harmless can be destructive, while things that seem disastrous can make a positive turnaround when left in God's hands. Sometimes, it's simply a matter of perspective. As you go into this study, pray that God will help you see your life from His eternal perspective.
overview: How God is faithful to finish what HE starts in your life.
How our attitudes through difficult time can attract unbelievers to Christ.
How God will fulfil His plans in spite of the motives and intentions of people.
The responsibility and privilege of Christians to stand for, as well as suffer for, their faith and identification with Christ.

discussion.heading: People in Process
discussion.intro: Read Php 1:3-6. Note that while appreciating the Philippian church for their support to his ministry, Paul was confident not only in what God has done for the people in saving them, but also what He will continue to do for them as they remain faithful to God and His work.

questions.text: Why do people sometimes start things that they don't finish?
If God has the ability to finish everything, why are people "incomplete" in so many ways? Why does He take people through a process?
questions.leader_note: Note: People develop stronger character, faith, and understanding through various life experiences.

questions.text: How should God's promise and ability to finish affect our attitude toward ourselves and others?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It should make us more patient and keep us from passing premature judgment on people's ability, character, or motives. God's promise should also make us more hopeful.

questions.text: Read Php 1:12-14. Often, when people suffer or are persecuted for a cause, others are emboldened to take up the cause as well. Why is this, when it might seem more logical that fear would drive people away or cause them to keep quiet?
Describe forms of persecution that you or other Christians might experience and how God's kingdom can advance as a result.
Read Php 1:15-19. Why is it so easy to be envious of another Christian's successes or opportunities? How is that attitude destructive and immature?
How can we maintain good attitude toward those who seem to be more "blessed"? How can we become better at promoting the gifts and ministries of others?
questions.leader_note: Note: God doesn't respect one person's faith or productivity more than another's, as long as each is being and doing what God intended.

questions.text: Read Php 1:19-26. Why does the prospect of death frighten most people? Why should it be different for a Christian?
How should the inevitability of death affect our lives currently?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We should live life to the fullest, not worrying about things that will eventually be meaningless. We should be more deliberate in influencing others toward Christ since they could die without Christ at any time.

discussion.heading: Purposeful Pain

questions.text: Read Php 1:27-30. Describe some of the positive results of Christians suffering for their faith.

discussion.note: Suffering for our faith doesn't mean we have done something wrong. The opposite is often true – it may verify that we have been faithful.

lessons.act: Spend a few moments in prayer, asking God to work things out in your life for His own glory and help you keep a good attitude in the meantime.

lessons.title: Change Your Priorities

memory_verse.text: Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ

getting_started: Our priorities often change from one stage of life to the next. In the near future, many of the things that are important to us presently would likely be replaced by other concerns. But no matter how our lives and priorities change, as Christians, we must be careful always to place Jesus first. In a world of compromise and flimsy commitments, we must resolve like the apostle Paul, to devote ourselves fully to Christ.
overview: No one can earn a relationship with God.
Nothing in life – even the good – compares to a relationship with Jesus.
To put aside things that distract us from following Christ.

questions.text: Read Php 3:1-6. Why do you think the apostle issued such stern warning in this passage?
questions.leader_note: Note: God's grace and faith in Christ is the basis of salvation, not human efforts.

questions.text: Read Titus 3:3-7. Why can't our own efforts be the basis of salvation or a personal relationship with God? Who makes the relationship possible?
Read Php 3:8-9. Why does Paul consider all things to be like rubbish or trash in order to develop His relationship with Jesus?

Think for a moment about all the energy you will expend in life – working, playing, getting an education, developing relationships. What difference would all these things make if you don't somehow fulfil and advance God's purposes?
Read Php 3:10-11. How can we personally apply in our lives this expression: "...know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings"?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We must seek to know Jesus through personal experience, and follow in His footsteps – living a life characterized by hope and power. We must seek to wholeheartedly serve God at all cost. And just like Paul, we must consider it a privilege to suffer for the cause of Christ.

questions.text: Read Php 3:12-16. How can forgetting the past help us to strive toward a better future? What kinds of things do we need to forget?
questions.leader_note: Note: It's difficult to move ahead spiritually while dwelling on past failures or reveling in our own accomplishments.

questions.text: What does verse 16 mean when it says in NIV to "live up to what we have already attained"?
Read Php 3:17-21. According to this passage, what's the motivation to keep walking in faith?

invitation_option.label: Invitation Option
invitation_option.text: The world offers nothing of lasting value. But when we accept Christ, we can gain everything that God has to offer. If you haven't yet accepted Christ into your life, do so now. See pg2 (AC.CONFIRMATION) for guidance.
invitation_option.note: A vital relationship with Christ is the most important thing in life.

lessons.act: List on a paper the things you do in a typical day. Beside each item listed, estimate the amount of time you spend on that activity. Then rate each activity in terms of importance on a scale from one to ten, with one being the least important and ten being the most important. What does each activity reveals about your priorities? Are you where you should be? Where does God fit in? Note that we often invest time and energy in things that have no lasting value while neglecting God's plans for our lives. Now, on the other side of your paper, describe three adjustments you could make in your priorities to place greater emphasis on developing closer relationships with Christ. Resolve to begin making these changes this week. Spend a few moments in prayer, asking God to help you in your commitments.

lessons.title: Change Your Focus

memory_verse.text: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit, but in humility consider others better than yourselves. Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others

getting_started: The work that the Lord Jesus did, which culminated in our salvation, is more than a cause for celebration; it's a cause for transformation. The new life He bequeathed us should affect every part of our daily lives and be evident to everyone around us. His was a life of humility and servanthood, which teaches us, among the other things, to set aside the concerns of our own lives for the good of others. This study emphasizes the need for the character traits of humility and servanthood to be evident in our lives.
overview: How thinking and acting like Jesus means considering others before ourselves.
How Jesus' sacrifice should influence our willingness to sacrifice for others.
How the new life we receive from Jesus enables us to live for Him and serve others.

questions.text: Read Php 2:1-2. What does it mean to be "like-minded"? Why is it important among Christians?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Individual Christians will have many different viewpoints and perspectives, but they need to be united in purpose to effectively communicate Christ's message.

questions.text: As Christians, how should our faith affect our relationships?
questions.leader_note: Hint: By definition, a Christian is a disciple of Christ. As His disciples, we should strive to treat others as Jesus did.

questions.text: Read Php 2:3-5. What does it mean to consider others better than ourselves? What would happen if everyone did this?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It means giving others as much consideration as we would give ourselves. It means everyone was looking out for the good of everyone else. Most people would have their needs met and feel a renewed sense of purpose.

questions.text: Read John 13:1-3,5,12-17. What was Jesus trying to teach His disciples by washing their feet?
questions.leader_note: Note: This act illustrated the importance of serving one another in humility and love.

questions.text: Read Php 2:12-13. What do you think it means to "work out your salvation with fear and trembling"?
questions.leader_note: Note: This passage doesn't mean we have to work "for" our salvation. Paul is writing to those he already calls "saints in Christ Jesus" (Php 1:1).

questions.text: What kinds of "good works" should be a natural part of a Christian's life?
questions.leader_note: Note: becoming more like Jesus is a process, not just a one-time event. While it's true that we receive salvation at a specific time, we are continually in the process of being perfected.

questions.text: What does it mean in verse 13 that God "works in you to will and to act according to his good pleasure"?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Both the desire and the act come from God.

questions.text: Read Php 2:14-16. According to this passage, what must Christians avoid in order to stand out in a positive way from others in the world? Why?
questions.leader_note: Hint: The passage cautions against complaining, which often makes people stand out in a negative way. When Christians complain unjustly or become argumentative, they may unintentionally communicate that their desires are more important than those of others. Such attitude can also indicate a lack of trust in God to work things for His good purpose. It reveals a focus that is on circumstances rather than on the Lord.

lessons.act: Get yourself paper and pen or pencil. Write "What would Jesus do differently…" at the top of the page. Then write the phrase "at home," "at school," "at work," and "with friends" down the left side. In each category, think of one issue that you have been dealing with and write a brief explanation of how Jesus might want you to handle it. Take a few minutes to pray, asking God's help to put your intentions into action, and the grace to serve others.

invitation_option.label: Invitation Option
invitation_option.text: If you have not yet received the gift of eternal life that Jesus died and rose to provide, make that decision now. See pg2 (ABC of Salvation) for guidance.

daily_dew_drops.title: The Sanctifier and the Sanctified Are One

lessons.title: Change Your Attitude

memory_verse.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus

getting_started: Bad attitudes so permeate our culture that we almost don't notice them – in others or in ourselves. We are often lured to parrot most people's complaints on how things seem not to be working on almost every facet of our society. But God is able to strengthen us with His joy and bring us peace and contentment. This study challenges us to rely more fully on God – the One who not only is in control, but loves us completely.
overview: How joy is a source of strength for Christians.
How prayer and dependence on God help relieve stress and anxiety.
What kinds of thoughts and actions bring inner peace.
The way to find and appreciate the value of contentment in all situations.

questions.text: Read Php 4:4-5. Paul was thrown into jail for faithfully preaching about Jesus. How was Paul able to stay joyful?
questions.leader_note: Note: Many people would have reacted with complaining, anger, or frustration. But by focusing on God rather than the circumstances, Paul was able to anticipate the good that could come out of unpleasant circumstances.

questions.text: What does Paul mean when he says, "Let your gentleness be evident to all" (v5, NIV)? Why does he then remind the Philippians that the Lord is near?
Why is an attitude of joy important for Christians?
questions.leader_note: Note: Maintaining an attitude of joy is one way to point others to Christ. But it's important for our own peace of mind as well.

questions.text: Read Neh 8:10. When do we usually feel strong spiritually? Determined according to how we think we're doing leads us to a wrong conclusion about true spiritual strength.

Take time read the following passages and identify reasons for joy mentioned in each passage: Psalms 13:5-6; 16:11; 81:1; 92:4-5; 105:3-4; Luke 1:47-48; Acts 5:41-42; Romans 5:1-2; 1 John 1:3-4. List additional reasons for Christians to have joy.
questions.leader_note: Note: The source of real joy is greater than ourselves, and it never changes. It is found in Christ alone.

questions.text: Read Php 4:6-7. What does this passage suggest to relieve stress? Is this a simplistic answer? Why or why not?
How can prayer relieve us of stress?
Read Php 4:10-13. How can a Christian learn to be content in all circumstances? What kinds of thoughts and priorities help?

The phrase "I can do everything through him who gives me strength" (v13, NIV) is often quoted in relation to accomplishing great things for God. But in the context of this passage, what is it really telling us?

lessons.act: Prayfully consider the following questions: 1. How can you take time this week to rejoice in God's goodness? 2. How can you maintain an attitude of peace during tough times? 3. Where have you been looking for fulfillment and contentment? How can you shift your focus and begin trusting God for these things? Pray, asking God to help you choose attitudes that glorify Him.

invitation_option.label: Invitation Option
invitation_option.text: If you haven't yet received God's gift of forgiveness and eternal life, you can receive it even now, so you too can experience the peace that a relationship with Jesus brings. See pg2 (ABC of Salvation) for guidance.

lessons.title: Positively Different

memory_verse.text: But he which hath called you is holy in all manner of conversation; Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy

getting_started: This study addresses some deep spiritual concepts in understandable and extremely practical terms. It is designed to give you a firm awareness of the standards to which God calls His people, how He helps them achieve those standards, and what effect His standards can have on them. As you go through this study, assess your own attitudes and behaviours, and resolve to live by a higher standard, even as you make holiness a norm in your life.
overview: How and why God calls His people to be different from those who don't know Him.
What it means in practical terms to be holy.
How we can develop true righteousness and holiness in our lives.

discussion.heading: Sanctified: Set Apart for a Purpose

questions.text: Read John 17:15-19. Sanctified. What do you think this spiritual sounding term means?
questions.leader_note: Note: While there needs to be clear break from wrong behaviours, a Christian must continue to overcome selfish desires and become more like Jesus (2 Cor 3:18).

questions.text: Read 2 Cor 6:17-18. What do you think it means to come out from or be separated from the world?
questions.leader_note: Note: There should be a clear contrast in character and conduct between those who follow Christ and those who reject Him.

questions.text: Read the following verses and point out the effort, conditions, and how we get fit for God's purpose: Isa 64:6; Gal 2:21; 1 Peter 2:24; Romans 9:30-32.
questions.leader_note: Note: We can stay right with God only by trusting Him, obeying His Word, and following His plans for our lives.

questions.text: Read Titus 2:11-14. For Christ's followers, what should be the motivation for doing right?
Read 2 Tim 1:9; Heb 12:14. What do you think it means to be holy?
questions.leader_note: Note: God intends His people to be holy. Holiness implies separation from worldly ways and the developing of a preference for positive actions. God's character – not human effort – is the basis for holiness.

questions.text: Read Eph 4:22-24. How do we become (or how does God make us) holy? What does it mean to "put off your old self" and "put on the new self"?
Read Lev 10:10. What do you think it means to "distinguish between the holy and the common"?
questions.leader_note: Note: Those seeking holiness must practice different attitudes, desires, and behaviours than what's "normal" in the world.

questions.text: What are some ideas, behaviours, activities, etc. that are "common" in the world but not appropriate choices for Christians?
questions.leader_note: Note: We must learn to discern what kinds of activities are acceptable for us as we try to imitate God.

questions.text: Read Romans 6:6-7, 11-14. What does it mean to "count yourself dead to sin"?
questions.leader_note: Hint: To be dead to sin is to be unresponsive to it. Instead, become more and more responsible and alive to God, doing what pleases Him.

lessons.act: Read Col 3:1-15. This passage is sometimes referred to as "Rules for Holy Living." Many people regard "holiness" as a huge constraint, pertaining to all the things Christians can't or shouldn't do. But the passage you just read contains more positive actions that it does negative restrictions. Although the things God tells us to avoid are more than reasonable and clearly for our good, the positive acts also benefit others. Note: Read 1 Peter 1:13-16. Holiness is active, not passive. If we pursue all the positive actions God gives us the opportunity to do, we'll have little time or desire to get caught up in the negative behaviours He commands us to avoid.

daily_dew_drops.title: Freed from the Curse of the Law

lessons.title: Truly Authentic Character

memory_verse.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known

getting_started: This study will help you define and consider what it means to have integrity. No single issue defines personal character more than the issue of integrity. Throughout the Bible, righteous people claimed to have, and were commended by God for, their integrity. In this study, you'll see how this crucial character trait can make all the difference in sustaining the high standards to which God calls His people.
overview: Several definitions of integrity and how they apply to the Christian life.
The consequences of a personal lack of integrity.
How integrity brings stability and success according to God's standards.

discussion.heading: Keeping It Together: Complete
discussion.intro: Read Job 1:1,6-2:10. Job maintained such a righteous life that God commended him above anyone else on earth. When Satan challenged Job's loyalty as self-serving, God allowed Satan to test Job.

questions.text: In what ways are teens – particularly Christian teens – pressured to compromise their integrity?
Why do people give in to these pressures? What do they hope to gain?
questions.leader_note: Hint: People are often willing to compromise their standards if they think that something will bring them pleasure, popularity, or convenience.

questions.text: Read Psalms 25:21; 26:1. According to these passages, what enables us to maintain integrity and be blameless?
questions.leader_note: Hint: When we put our hope and trust in God, He helps us "keep it together." We must rely on Him for strength.

questions.text: Read Luke 6:47-49. What was the main difference between the two … [page 052 not supplied]

lessons.title: Losing Your I.D.
lessons.text: Psalms 119:32; Mark 8:34-38; John 14:15; Romans 16:19; 1 Thess 5:21-22; 1 Tim 6:11; 2 Tim 2:22; 3 John 11

memory_verse.text: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me

getting_started: It has been said that others determine your reputation, but you determine your character. While it is possible to be known for so many things as a teen, even the most desirable reputations are often built on things that may not really matter after your teen years. As a believer, it's important not to let your true identity as a Christian get buried beneath less important things that won't last. So, as you go into this study, desire to be a shining example of what it means to follow Christ.
overview: What it means to "deny ourselves," how we do it, and what it means in regard to a relationship with Christ.
What it means to "take up our cross," and how it identifies us with Christ.
What it means to follow Christ and how we do it.

discussion.heading: Deny yourself…
discussion.intro: Following Jesus is an adventure. Rather than limiting the possibilities, serving Jesus opens up a world of possibilities.

questions.text: Read Mark 8:34-38. How can a relationship change one's attitudes, actions, and priorities – often taking precedence over all other things?
questions.leader_note: Hint: For a Christian, an authentic relationship with Jesus mean more than anything.

questions.text: Read Romans 16:19. Why is it important to heed Apostle Paul's admonition that we be uninformed or inexperienced regarding evil?
questions.leader_note: Note: The devil cannot use certain things (e.g., drugs, alcohol, pornography, sexual activity, destructive friendships, etc.,) against you if you've chosen not to expose yourself to the temporary "thrill" of those activities.

questions.text: Read Mark 8:35. What does it mean to "lose" your life? How can that help you find it?
questions.leader_note: Hint: In a world that serves itself, God rewards those who serve Him.

questions.text: Read Matthew 2:1-8, 16. Why would some people view Jesus as a threat?
What should the cross mean to Christians?
questions.leader_note: Note: Jesus gave His life for a world that rejects Him. He identified with us so we can identify with Him.

questions.text: How are Christians often identified? How should they be?
questions.leader_note: Note: As Christians we should strive for an identity wrapped up in a relationship with Christ.

questions.text: Why do you think that certain people give Christians a hard time?
questions.leader_note: Note: The people who despise and harass Christians the most are usually searching for something. But before they risk believing for themselves, they put Christians to the test – trying to get them to lay down their cross – to see if what they profess to have is worth persecution.

discussion.heading: Follow Christ
discussion.note: Some Christian teens often test the bounds of right and wrong. They mistakenly assume that they can put themselves into tempting situations and still have strength to resist. When they fail, they feel guilty.

questions.text: Read 1 Thess 5:21-22; 3 John 11. According to this passage, what does "following Jesus" imply?
Read 1 Tim 6:11; 2 Tim 2:22. What do these passages tell us about handling temptation? What do these passages tell us about … [text unclear in photo]
questions.leader_note: Hint: We cannot put ourselves in compromising situations and assume we will not give in.

questions.text: Read Psalm 119:32; John 14:15. What is the best motivation for doing what's right – especially for a Christian?
questions.leader_note: Hint: doing what's right out of obligation or duty can lead to weariness and short-lived commitments. But a relationship with Jesus frees us to do right and act rightly in love.

lessons.title: Be A Giver

memory_verse.text: But whoso hath this world's good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?

getting_started: The act of generosity might seem like a simple concept, however giving can too easily be simplified into the act of offering someone else money or materials. However, Jesus also called us to be givers of time, compassion, and love. As such, generosity isn't just about what is true internally of a person, but has outward expression in giving. Through prayer it also pertains to the needs of the heart. And through prayer, we can choose to be even as we remain open to the Spirit's leading in how, when, and to whom we give.
overview: Why Christians are asked to give.
To whom Christians should give.
How Christians should give.

questions.text: Read 1 John 3:16-18. What does giving mean to you?
questions.leader_note: Note: Generosity is a tangible way to show God's love to others. Thus, true generosity is love in action – with no expectations attached.

questions.text: What do you think is meant by, "let us not love with words, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth"? (1 John 3:18, KJV)
questions.leader_note: Hint: Encouraging words can be helpful to someone in need. However, words alone aren't always helpful. For example, offering a kind word or uplifting Scripture to someone who is starving is not the appropriate response. In that scenario, the Bible teaches us to take care of the obvious need first.

questions.text: Read Proverbs 19:17. What do you think "lend" means in this verse?
questions.leader_note: Note: When we show generosity to others, it's like a loan to God. God says that He will repay that loan one day. Whether during this life or the next, God will reward a generous heart.

discussion.heading: To whom should I give?
discussion.note: Ultimately, a key part of the life of Christians should be the desire to help others. When we see others through the eyes of Christ, it's easy to feel compassionate mercy

questions.text: Read Luke 10:25-37. To whom should we give? Are we instructed to give only to those around us? To family? To other Christians?
Luke 10:37 uses the word "mercy." Why do you think that word was used?

discussion.heading: How should I give?
discussion.note: Generosity starts with the heart. A generous spirit only matures by allowing God's love to flow in us and through us. By learning to see through God's spiritual lens we can be true extensions and conduits of His love. God's message is clear. We are to complete the mission that Christ began.

questions.text: Read 1 Tim 6:18-19. What does generosity mean to you? How would you say generosity might differ from giving?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Generosity goes beyond giving – it is an overwhelming need to help someone. While giving itself is simply an action.

questions.text: Read 2 Cor 9:6-8. What do you think it means to sow and reap in this passage? How would you describe a "cheerful giver"?

lessons.act: Read Proverbs 10:9. In what ways can integrity keep a person secure? In what ways will a lack of integrity catch up with a person or be revealed? [Note: Developing and maintaining strong personal integrity will mean putting up with some tough times, but it will keep you close to God and His perfect purpose for your life. Conversely, deceitful attitudes lead to moral and ethical failure.] Pray, asking God to strengthen you in your resolve to live a life of integrity.

lessons.title: Responding to God's Gift

memory_verse.text: He was in the world, and though the world was made through him, the world did not recognize him… Yet to all who received him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God

getting_started: For Christians, Christmas is a time to reflect on God's greatest gift. It's more than a celebration of a life and an opportunity to honour Jesus. But much of the world views it as little more than a season of indulgence, rushing to and from the market or from one social event to the next. While most of these people may have good intentions, Christ is sadly absent from their celebrations.

Just like Christmas, since Jesus first came to earth, people's responses have ranged from contempt to contentment – from cynicism to celebration. This study will help you recognize positive ways to respond to Jesus, and also guide you to respond accordingly.
overview: The variety of attitudes and actions people display in response to Jesus.
The positive ways we can respond to Jesus and His message.
Why it's important to understand and appreciate the different ways people worship Jesus.

discussion.heading: Attitudes
discussion.note: Joseph's attitude shows that it really takes faith to accept and live for Jesus.

questions.text: Read Luke 2:25-32. How did Simeon's attitude about the promise of Jesus' coming impact his life?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It caused him to trust God and to remain sensitive to God's direction.

questions.text: How could an attitude of greater anticipation toward Christ change your life?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It could cause you to become more focused on doing the things that lead you into His presence.

questions.text: Read Matt 1:18-25. How did Joseph's attitude change when the angel appeared to Him?
Read Luke 2:7. What are some things that overcrowd people's lives or keep them from making room for Jesus?
Why do you think some people refuse to take Christ seriously, even though they believe He is Lord?
questions.leader_note: Hint: People get so caught up in their own lives and concerns, making excuses for not being faithful to God. Some put off serving Him with the intention of making deeper commitment later.

questions.text: Read Luke 2:8-18. How do you usually act toward someone who wants to talk about his or her relationship with God constantly? Why?
questions.leader_note: Note: Like those shepherds, some people are very vocal about their faith. It's important we respect everyone's way of responding to Jesus, even if it isn't how we would respond.

questions.text: Read Luke 2:19. Do you think it's more or less spiritual to respond to God either with loud praise or quiet contemplation? Why?
questions.leader_note: Note: Instead of focusing on conforming to certain outward mannerism, we should rather work on our inner man – ensure our lives conform perfectly to the image of Christ and completely yielded to His will.

questions.text: Read Luke 2:36-40. How should our relationship with God affect our attitude toward other Christians?
questions.leader_note: Hint: Like Ann, we should make a point of encouraging each other. After all, we've experienced the greatest news possible: Our Saviour has come to change our lives.

lessons.act: Ask God to search your heart and reveal any negative responses toward Him in your life. It may be apathy (i.e., simply not caring about God's priorities) in a certain area, or being angry toward God for circumstance you don't understand. Ask forgiveness for these attitudes and allow God to replace the negative with godly responses that honour Him.

reach_out.label: Reach Out
reach_out.text: Do a service project as a gift to Jesus. Dress an elderly neighbours' compound, help take down decorations, or do a sibling's chores for them without complaining.

lessons.title: Radical Commitment

memory_verse.text: …any of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be my disciple

getting_started: As teens, we're at a time in our lives when temptation and peer pressure are mounting, and the sacrifices involved in selling out to God are likely becoming more apparent. We're equally at a time in our lives when most of us are weighing different options, as we search for a cause worthy for our lives – a cause that will deliver to us a future that we can be glad of. To really achieve that great future, we must take strong action to respond positively to the challenge of total commitment, which Jesus presents to us in today's study. As we do, our lives will take on the meaning, purpose, and adventure God intends for us.
overview: Why it's essential to rid our lives of sin so as not to mislead others.
How identifying with Jesus carries a price, and how our lives are affected when His mission becomes our mission.
The kinds of sacrifices and choices we'll make if following Jesus is truly our highest priority.
How nothing in our lives – no other relationship or endeavour – should compare to our relationship with Christ.

questions.text: Read Mark 9:42. What do you think Jesus is trying to tell us in this verse?
Read Mark 9:43-48. Why do you think Jesus said what He said in this verse?
questions.leader_note: Note: The three body parts mentioned in Jesus' illustration are all controlled by the will. So, Jesus was talking about our choices and desires. Being a follower of Jesus must change us on the inside.

questions.text: What's the penalty for letting sin rule in our lives?
questions.leader_note: Note: Jesus calls us to reject anything that could prevent us from following Him. These can be hard sacrifice to make, but they'll be worth it. Following Him must be our highest priority.

questions.text: Read Matt 2:1-8, 16. Why would some people view Jesus as a threat?
Read John 6:53-57. What does this passage reveal about Jesus' identity and how to identify with Him?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We must identify how Jesus wants us to identify with Him and what He stands for by giving our lives totally to His service. His mission becomes our mission in every way.

questions.text: Read Luke 14:25-27. Does Jesus really want us to hate people – especially those closest to us? Why or why not?
questions.leader_note: Note: Our commitment to Jesus must be greater than anything else in our lives – including what's closest and dearest to us, such as our families.

questions.text: Read Luke 14:28-33. What resources do you think the men in the stories had at their disposal?
What resources do we have to fulfill our commitment to Christ and His mission? What does it mean to give these things up?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We have money, time, talents, etc. "Giving them up" means putting aside our own plans so we can use them however He desires. But we also have spiritual resources: God's power, the Bible, and direction from the Holy Spirit. Because of these resources we can be sure that our total commitment is well spent. God will help us accomplish whatever He wants us to do.

lessons.act: Make a list of things you need to avoid to keep from misleading people and to keep you away from temptation. Your list may include people, places, things, and activities. Keep the list in your pocket or locker this week. Clean your room and your locker. Make sure to remove anything that might cause you to consider doing something that would violate God's standards.

reach_out.label: Reach Out
reach_out.text: Is the example you set every day pleasing to God and beneficial to others? Ask God to reveal areas of your life that could be stumbling blocks for others. Rid your life of anything that could hurt your witness for God.
